basis: Read-only inspection of the canonical checkout (D:/trading-agent-dashboard-codex, branch main-published) and the strategy worktree. Every number below was read from the file named in evidence; none is inferred from prose.

paths.note: evidence paths are relative to the repository root; a study marked published:false is absent from origin/main and readable only in the canonical checkout or the worktree

reach_97.definition: A call is a reach hit when price travels half the standard L2L distance (standard = ADR20 x 0.5, half = ADR20 x 0.25) in the called direction at any point inside the date-keyed source session attached to evaluation_inputs.close_date. Exact equality counts. There is no adverse boundary, no entry, no stop and no sequencing, so it is a reach rate, not a win rate.
reach_97.not: not directional accuracy, not a win rate, not evidence of reliability, not an executable result (prohibited by data/l2l-directional-research-verdict-v1.json)

gate_0_of_725.definition: Legacy gate ladder in data/usd-layer1-backtester/run-v1.json validity_gate.ladder: present 618/725, fresh 617/725, clocked 0/725, identified 0/725 (directional-call scope: 451, 450, 0, 0 of 515).
gate_0_of_725.meaning: The failure is the observation time and identity of stored inputs, not missing rows: 618 sessions hold the values, none carries a recorded as-of time, so neither later rung can be reached.

studies.question: Does replaying the archived USD call reproduce the published call, direction and factor arguments?
studies.metric: row parity (pass / exact_match) over the archive; horizon 'following 24hrs' (next 16:00 ET)
studies.outcome: 604 pass, 0 fail, 0 missing_data; 603 exact matches
studies.reuse: archived corpus of published calls; the only per-call input to calibration; never present as an accuracy result

studies.question: Same parity question for GOLD.
studies.metric: row parity; horizon following 24hrs
studies.outcome: 608 pass, 608 exact
studies.reuse: archived corpus; calibration input

studies.question: Same parity question for EUR.
studies.metric: row parity; horizon following 24hrs
studies.outcome: 602 pass, 602 exact
studies.reuse: archived corpus; calibration input

studies.question: Same parity question for NQ (QQQ proxy benchmark).
studies.metric: row parity; horizon following 24hrs
studies.outcome: 604 pass, 604 exact
studies.reuse: archived corpus; calibration input

studies.question: Same parity question for BTC.
studies.metric: row parity; horizon following 24hrs
studies.outcome: 850 pass, 850 exact
studies.reuse: archived corpus; calibration input

studies.question: Inside the session attached to the call, how often did price travel the full standard L2L distance and half of it in the called direction?
studies.metric: reach rate; full target ADR20 x 0.5, half target ADR20 x 0.25; exact equality counts; no adverse boundary, no entry, no stop
studies.reuse: reuse the definitions and paths; the 97 % may not be quoted as accuracy, win rate or reliability and must carry its definition (see figures.reach_97)

studies.question: How often does the full L2L 1H-sequence distance get reached in the following 24 hours, and how does that move with the threshold?
studies.metric: l2lRangeAvailablePct, full distance only, horizon following 24hrs
studies.denominator: EUR 570 evaluated calls (per-asset tables for GOLD, NQ, BTC, plus layer 2 pairs)
studies.outcome: EUR 72.3 % (412 reach / 158 no reach); Strong+ subset 73 % on 126 calls; 5 sessions missing intraday data
studies.reuse: threshold-sensitivity tables are the reusable part and are cleared for publication; the headline is superseded by half-l2l-reach-v2

studies.question: Does each Layer 1 or Layer 2 call predict the open-to-close direction of its designated trading session?
studies.metric: directional accuracy of the open-to-close label; chronological folds; always-bullish baseline per fold
studies.reuse: reusable population and fold design; the result is negative and the final test is consumed

studies.question: Does the called side reach more often than the opposite side, on the same calls?
studies.metric: paired called-minus-opposite reach, McNemar; both half and full distance
studies.outcome: layer 1 -2.61 pp at half distance and -3.17 pp at full; layer 2 -1.76 pp both; bearish layer 1 full reach 37.35 % vs opposite 44.49 % (p 0.0076); conclusion BEARISH_ASYMMETRY_ONLY
studies.reuse: negative; the paired design is reusable for any future call set, the conclusion forbids any direction-skill claim

studies.question: Why do the calls fail to beat a naive baseline, and is the failure concentrated?
studies.metric: excess accuracy vs baseline; bullish vs bearish accuracy; confidence monotonicity
studies.denominator: same 4,085 rows; folds as in l2l-trading-day-directional-v1
studies.outcome: excess vs baseline -5.54 pp layer 1 and -5.46 pp layer 2; layer 2 adds 0 over matched layer 1; bullish 50.69/51.12 % vs bearish 42.96/42.33 %; confidence not monotone in either layer
studies.reuse: negative; the bearish underperformance is the one stable signal and is a diagnostic, not an edge

studies.question: What may be claimed from the whole L2L chain?
studies.metric: frozen summary of hashed artefacts
studies.outcome: validatedPredictorOfDesignatedSessionDirection false; original 96.99/70.52 (L1) and 97.3/72.3 (L2) declared ORIGINAL_METRIC_PATH_DEPENDENT; four prohibited claims listed
studies.reuse: the prohibition text must be carried by any new surface; this is the authority on what may not be said

studies.question: Is the failure an implementation defect or a horizon mismatch?
studies.metric: code-path trace plus exact reproduction of stored directions
studies.denominator: same 4,085 rows; stored directions reproduced exactly
studies.outcome: bestExplainedBy horizon_mismatch; no defect in the call logic; the excursion metric answers a different question than session direction
studies.reuse: read before any attempt to repair the calls: it says the machinery is not broken

studies.question: Why does the same population score 97 % under the reach builder and 64.34 % under a session-anchored walk?
studies.metric: transition matrix between the two reach definitions; path-dependence counts
studies.outcome: ORIGINAL_METRIC_PATH_DEPENDENT; 1,325 original-only half hits, of which 1,207 carry a later initiating swing; the original headline reproduces exactly (2,418/75 and 1,549/43)
studies.reuse: the authority for why the 97 % figure may not travel alone; cite it beside the definition

studies.question: Could a session-close predictor be built from information available before the session opens?
studies.metric: input timing audit; feature availability status per row
studies.outcome: INPUT_TIMING_NOT_DEFENSIBLE; many features are date-only or end-of-day reconstructions while sessions open the same date at 22:00-23:00Z; no untouched holdout exists locally
studies.reuse: the timing audit is directly reusable as the requirements list for a 05:00 London dataset

studies.question: What would an executable half-distance entry test need?
studies.metric: entry scenarios, OHLC sequencing rules, cost model, evaluation design
studies.outcome: status DRAFT_BLOCKED_FROM_PROFITABILITY_EXECUTION; blocked on approved costs and on 5-minute sequencing data
studies.reuse: reuse the design as the spec for the first genuine backtest; it is a plan, not a result

studies.question: Which single factor carried the 24-hour call, and did its vote match the outcome?
studies.metric: per-factor directional outcome, ex-flat win rate; strongest/weakest factor per asset
studies.denominator: USD 604 observations across 10 factors (plus EUR, Gold, NQ, BTC blocks)
studies.outcome: single-factor survey only, no combined headline; USD strongest bullish F10 Equity Regime 62.5, strongest bearish F2 US 2Y Yield Delta 56.9, weakest F7 Economic Surprise -45.5; ADR/L2L join marked unavailable
studies.reuse: factor-by-factor descriptive table; not a ranking and not a weight proposal

studies.question: Does stated confidence match realised hit rate, by market, direction and bucket?
studies.metric: ex-flat win rate per 10-point confidence bucket; calibration gap; chronological fold consistency; sample-size tiers
studies.denominator: layer 1 pooled 3,268 rows / 3,094 directional calls (2,941 resolved: 1,066 correct, 894 wrong, 981 flat); layer 2 874 / 821 resolved (322 / 252 / 247)
studies.outcome: layer 1 54.39 % ex-flat, layer 2 56.10 %; bucket 90-100 holds 14 calls; bearish trails bullish inside a bucket (30-39: 42.7 % vs 56.8 %); no monotone ladder
studies.reuse: the labelling vocabulary (bucket, tier, gap, fold) is reusable as-is; the accuracies belong to the 16:00 ET horizon and must not be compared with session-close numbers

studies.question: What may a band be labelled, and when must it say 'insufficient evidence'?
studies.metric: 330 band rows across exact-market and market-band scopes; sample-size thresholds; fallback hierarchy
studies.denominator: 330 rows; thresholds 0-9 very limited, 10-29 limited, 30-99 reasonable, 100+ substantial
studies.outcome: delivery contract plus a reconciliation block; no new accuracy claim
studies.reuse: use verbatim for any confidence display; the thresholds are the reason a 14-call bucket cannot be shown as a band

studies.question: Would a shadow book have beaten the live book?
studies.metric: ex-flat win rate, shadow vs live, per asset
studies.outcome: claims +23 pp pooled; family detail 2 improved, 0 degraded, 3 mixed
studies.reuse: non-authoritative; do not publish the +23 pp until the pooling and the per-market weighting are re-derived

studies.window: 154 stored calls, calendar split at 2026-08-01; 76,143 one-hour candles
studies.question: Does the stored Gold call record beat always-bullish on a 24-hour horizon?
studies.metric: directional accuracy ex-flat; two evaluation lanes (strict 24 elapsed hours, endpoint from next minute to next 16:00); always-bullish baseline on the same scored calls
studies.denominator: 154 calls; strict lane 0 evaluable; endpoint lane 97 evaluable (45 correct, 37 wrong, 13 flat)
studies.outcome: endpoint 54.88 % vs always-bullish 52.44 % on 82 scored calls; training slice 60 evaluable at 68 %; validation slice 37 evaluable at 34.38 % vs 59.38 % baseline; untouched_holdout_claimed false
studies.reuse: raw stored calls and the two-lane design are reusable; the 54.88 % is not stable across the split and must not be quoted alone

studies.question: Does a technical-analysis H1 rule set predict EUR/USD open-to-close direction better than always-long?
studies.metric: directional accuracy ex-flat per chronological fold; always-long baseline on the same folds
studies.denominator: folds 205 / 153 / 118 rows; dataset excludes 128 input records before feature construction
studies.outcome: validation 56.21 % vs 53.59 % baseline; final test 42.37 % vs 44.92 %; readyForDashboard false
studies.reuse: reusable as the worked example of a properly split test that failed; its dataset is not a 05:00 input source

studies.question: Status of the observation-first research pipeline.
studies.metric: counts only
studies.outcome: status document; no performance claim
studies.reuse: archive only; superseded by the l2l chain and the point-in-time replay

studies.question: What state is the XAU/USD engine in, and which research claim supports which gate?
studies.metric: status lanes, qualification gate, release gate
studies.denominator: 448 eligible directional calls on the engine lane
studies.outcome: full reach 73.2 % (328/448), half reach 99.1 % (444/448), data coverage 73.7 %, strength grade UNAVAILABLE; both files state they do not qualify live calls
studies.reuse: reusable as the release-gate vocabulary; its percentages are a different population from half-l2l-reach-v2 and must not be mixed

studies.question: Can the USD Layer 1 book be replayed point-in-time, morning by morning, under an auditable gate?
studies.metric: sessions replayed; gate ladder (present, fresh, clocked, identified); execution states
studies.denominator: 725 replayed sessions; 320 eligible; 196 directional calls; 62 trade-qualified
studies.outcome: present 618/725, fresh 617/725, clocked 0/725, identified 0/725; band counts 22/105/50/19/0; three mornings hit CAP-3
studies.reuse: the most reusable engine in the repository; the 0/725 is a label on this ladder, not a claim about model coverage

studies.question: Does the USD call predict the official cash DXY direction over the session?
studies.metric: direction agreement against official cash DXY
studies.outcome: blocked: no official cash DXY with a 05:00 quote in the checkout
studies.reuse: this is the missing-input list for the official benchmark, not a result

studies.question: Same question on the only dollar index available locally, a broker spot CFD.
studies.metric: direction agreement; lower bound reported
studies.outcome: status scored_proxy; current model 284 scored at 49.65 % (lower bound 43.88); challenger 205 scored at 42.93 %; challenger_v1 209 scored at 43.54 %
studies.reuse: usable as a proxy lane if every surface labels it a broker CFD; is_official_cash_dxy false

studies.model: run-v1 test 2 plus decision-rules-v1 scored blocks
studies.question: Using the USD call alone, how often did EUR/USD, XAU/USD, BTC/USD and NAS100 move opposite the call over the same session?
studies.metric: agreement with the inverted call; Wilson interval; per-market and joint
studies.denominator: 685 of 725 sessions priced; v1 book 196 calls; live-engine arm 439-536 scored per market
studies.reuse: reusable; never quote the 167-call arm (superseded run 9e4b8d5f) whose figures are 50.0/58.6/51.9/46.6 %

studies.question: Does the laddered L2L setup reach 5R (full) and 3R (half) with a defined entry, stop and sequence?
studies.metric: R-multiple outcome under OHLC sequencing
studies.outcome: blocked on two inputs: no 5-minute tape and no ladder archived before the setup
studies.reuse: the only tests that could speak to profitability are empty; do not substitute the reach studies for them

studies.question: Does the order plumbing work end to end?
studies.metric: fills and percentage change on a two-day EUR/USD 5-minute replay
studies.outcome: claims +6.97 %; the call direction was taken from the live fill record because no 05:00 archive exists for those mornings
studies.reuse: plumbing test only; never present as a backtest result

studies.question: What did the frozen nine-input rule book produce across 725 mornings?
studies.metric: execution states, rule failures, band counts, traded count
studies.outcome: 41 allowed, 541 blocked, 143 abstained; BULLISH 87, BEARISH 109, NO_CALL 529; 62 traded; failures E2 404, E3 297, E4 6, E5 529, E6 134
studies.reuse: the rule book is the component worth reusing; the state counts are descriptive and carry no edge

studies.question: Can a 17-feature logistic challenger beat the stored engine on a 24-hour direction target without tuning on the holdout?
studies.metric: holdout ex-flat accuracy with 95 % interval; 60 % target; pre-registered filters
studies.denominator: 583 evaluable rows; 93 configurations; 85 in pool; 0 passed the full filter, 2 passed the reduced filter; 80 decided holdout calls
studies.outcome: 46.25 % (CI 35.75-57.10) vs engine 52.78 % (CI 41.40-63.87); target_60_percent_met false; evidence_classification not_supported
studies.reuse: the registry and pre-registration pattern are the reusable part; the result is a clean negative
